user: A cylindrical tank of radius 0.324 is initially empty and is filled with water. For the first 34 minutes, inflow is 13.08 L/min; for the next 23 minutes it is 64.94 L/min. Outflow is 6.47 L/min throughout. At the end of each minute (after applying that minute’s inflow and outflow), if the water height exceeds 0.447, a sloshing loss of 13.9% of the excess volume above height 0.447 occurs instantly. Find the final water height and the total lost volume.
target_response:
<<<PLAN>>>
Goal: <ANS> = final water height in the tank after all minutes, and the total volume lost to sloshing over the whole process
Unknowns:
- <U1> = final water height after minute 57 (after that minute’s inflow, outflow, and any sloshing loss)
- <U2> = total accumulated sloshing-loss volume over minutes 1 through 57
Core constraints:
- <C1>: Tank is a right circular cylinder with radius given in the statement; water volume and water height are linked by the cylinder’s constant cross-sectional area.
- <C2>: The tank starts empty, so initial water volume is zero.
- <C3>: For minutes 1 through 34, inflow rate is the first value given; for minutes 35 through 57, inflow rate is the second value given; outflow rate is the given constant value for all minutes.
- <C4>: Each minute is processed in this order: add that minute’s inflow volume, subtract that minute’s outflow volume, then check height; if height exceeds the threshold height given, a sloshing loss occurs instantly equal to the given percentage of the “excess” volume above the threshold height (computed using the threshold height as the cutoff).
- <C5>: Total sloshing loss is the sum of all per-minute sloshing losses; final height is computed from the final post-slosh volume.
Dependency skeleton:
- <R1> from <C1>: Determine the tank’s cross-sectional area from the given radius, and the volume corresponding to the threshold height from the given threshold height.
- <R2> from <C2>, <C3>, <C4>, and <R1>: Define a minute-by-minute recurrence for post-slosh volume, using the correct inflow for that minute, constant outflow, and conditional sloshing based on whether the pre-slosh volume exceeds the threshold volume.
- <R3> from <C4> and <R2>: Define per-minute sloshing-loss volume as zero when below threshold, otherwise as the given fraction of the excess above threshold; accumulate these losses over all minutes.
- <R4> from <C1> and the final value produced by <R2>: Convert final post-slosh volume to final water height.
Plan:
- Identify the minimum set of intermediates needed for <ANS>: cylinder area, threshold volume, a running water volume updated once per minute, and a running total of slosh losses.
- Compute <R1>: cross-sectional area from the given radius; threshold volume from area and the given threshold height; ensure unit consistency between liters and the cylinder’s length units by applying the standard liters-to-cubic-length conversion consistent with the radius/height units.
- Compute <R2> and <R3> by iterating minutes 1 to 57:
  - For each minute, compute that minute’s inflow volume from the applicable inflow rate and one minute duration, compute that minute’s outflow volume from the constant outflow rate and one minute duration, update a pre-slosh volume by applying inflow then outflow.
  - Compare the pre-slosh volume to the threshold volume; if it exceeds, compute the excess volume above threshold, compute slosh loss as the given percentage of that excess, subtract this loss from the volume to get the post-slosh volume, and add the loss to the running total; otherwise keep volume unchanged and add zero loss.
- After finishing minute 57, compute <R4>: convert the final post-slosh volume to the final height using the cylinder area.
- Report <U1> as the final height from <R4>, and <U2> as the accumulated sloshing-loss total from <R3>.  
<<<END>>>
response:
<<<PLAN>>>
Goal: <ANS> = (final water height and total lost volume)
Unknowns:
- <U1>=final water height
- <U2>=total lost volume
Core constraints:
- <C1>: the tank is cylindrical with radius given in the statement
- <C2>: the tank is initially empty
- <C3>: inflow rate is given in the statement for the first 34 minutes and for the next 23 minutes
- <C4>: outflow rate is given in the statement throughout
- <C5>: after each minute, if the water height exceeds 0.447, a sloshing loss of 13.9% of the excess volume above height 0.447 occurs instantly
Dependency skeleton:
- <R1> from <C1> and <C2>: volume of the tank at any height
- <R2> from <C3> and <C4>: net inflow rate over each minute
- <R3> from <C5> and <R1>: sloshing loss per minute
- <R4> from <R2> and <R3>: total loss over each minute
- <R5> from <R1> and <R4>: cumulative volume at each minute
- <R6> from <R5> and <R1>: final water height
- <R7> from <R4> and <R1>: total lost volume
Plan:
- Identify the minimum set of intermediates needed for <ANS>: cumulative volume at each minute, total loss per minute, and final height.
- Compute <R1> as the volume of the tank at any height using the given radius.
- Compute <R2> as the net inflow rate over each minute by subtracting the outflow rate from the inflow rate for each time interval.
- Compute <R3> as the sloshing loss per minute by taking 13.9% of the excess volume above height 0.447.
- Compute <R4> as the total loss over each minute by summing <R3> for each minute.
- Compute <R5> as the cumulative volume at each minute by adding <R2> and <R4> to the initial volume.
- Compute <R6> as the final water height by finding the height corresponding to the cumulative volume at the end of the last minute.
- Compute <R7> as the total lost volume by summing <R4> over all minutes.

user: A drug concentration follows dC/dt = -0.231C between doses. You administer 7 identical bolus doses of size 37.22 at scheduled times t_i=(i-1)*3.74 hours for i=1..7. If concentration exceeds 44.51, you skip the next scheduled dose once. The planned total dose is exactly 260.54. Given k, H, and this schedule pattern, compute the final concentration at time 29.25 and how many doses were skipped.

Unknowns:

- <U2> = the final concentration at time 29.25 hours

- <C2>: At a dosing time that is administered, concentration jumps upward by the bolus dose size given in the statement
- <C3>: Dosing times are the scheduled times given in the statement for indices one through seven
- <C4>: After any administered dose, if the resulting concentration exceeds the threshold given in the statement, then the next scheduled dose is skipped; this skip rule can be applied at most once

- <R2> from <C1> and the final evaluation time given in the statement: the decay multiplier from the last administered dose time to time 29.25 (depends on which dose, if any, was skipped)
- <R3> from <C2>, <R1>, and the initial condition implied by the dosing process: a step-by-step recurrence giving the concentration immediately after each scheduled time, with the “administer versus skip” choice applied at the appropriate time
- <R4> from <R3> and <C4>: identification of <U1> by finding the first time (if any) the post-dose concentration exceeds the threshold, then flagging the immediately following scheduled dose as skipped (and ensuring no further skips)
- <R5> from <R3>, <R2>, and <U1>: the concentration at time 29.25 obtained by decaying forward from the last administered dose time to 29.25, yielding <U2>
Plan:
- Identify the minimum set of intermediates needed for <ANS>.
- Compute <R1> using the given decay rate and the fixed inter-dose interval from the schedule.
- Iterate through the scheduled times in order:
  - Start from the implied baseline concentration before the first dose.

  - After each administered bolus, compare the immediate post-dose concentration to the threshold to determine whether the next scheduled dose must be skipped, but only once total per <C4>.
- From this iteration, determine <U1> (none or a specific next-dose index) and thus the number of skipped doses.
- Determine the last administered dose time implied by <U1>, compute <R2> for the time gap from that last administered time to 29.25, and apply that decay to the concentration right after the last administered dose to obtain <U2>.
- Report <U2> and the skip count implied by <U1>.
